nodes.name: Carbon paper hydrophilic pretreatment
nodes.procedure: Prior to thermal shock, carbon paper (Toray TGP-H-060) underwent hydrophilic treatment by annealing at 450°C for 150 min. To ensure both structural stability and electrical conductivity throughout the synthesis process, we employed a combination of silver glue and copper tape to fix the carbon paper securely onto the glass plate.
nodes.source_text: Prior to thermal shock, carbon paper (Toray TGP-H-060) underwent hydrophilic treatment by annealing at 450°C for 150 min. To ensure both structural stability... copper tape to fix the carbon paper securely onto the glass plate.

nodes.name: Precursor solution preparation and impregnation
nodes.procedure: Iridium acetylacetonate (Ir(acac)₃) and yttrium nitrate hexahydrate (Y(NO₃)₃·6H₂O) precursors were meticulously mixed in a solvent comprising water and ethanol, with an overall loading of approximately 200 μL cm⁻². Specifically, solutions of Ir(acac)₃ and Y(NO₃)₃ were prepared at a concentration of 0.05 mol L⁻¹. The amalgamated solution, featuring a metal ion ratio of Ir:Y = 1:1, was directly sprayed onto pretreated carbon paper substrates measuring 6 cm in length and 2 cm in width.

nodes.procedure: Then, the carbon paper was directly employed for Joule heating experiments. To initiate thermal shock, a rapid electrical current was applied, thereby catalyzing phase transformations within the sample. nodes.source_text: We have applied IrY catalyst as the anode and the commercial Pt/C catalyst as the cathode to assemble a PEM electrolyzer... the IrY catalyst exhibits superior intrinsic activity when compared with the commercial IrO₂. nodes.characterization_summary: IrY maintained a pure Ir phase with face-centered cubic lattice structure; slight shift of diffraction peaks toward lower angles indicates lattice expansion after Y doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: after rare earth element doping, X-ray diffraction (XRD) results (Figure 1b) reveal that IrY maintained a pure Ir phase characterized by a face-centered cubic lattice structure... slight shift of the diffraction peaks toward lower angles manifests, thereby illustrating lattice expansion after Y doping.

nodes.characterization_summary: IrY nanoparticles evenly dispersed on carbon paper with sizes mainly 40-50 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analysis reveals that the IrY nanoparticles are evenly dispersed on carbon paper (Figure 1c), and the sizes of these nanoparticles mainly fall within the size range of 40 - 50 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-EDS mapping confirms uniform distribution of Y within the Ir lattice.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Further analysis was conducted using high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF) and corresponding energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping... confirms that the distribution of Y within the Ir lattice is strikingly uniform.

nodes.characterization_summary: Well-defined lattice fringes of 0.235 nm attributed to (111) plane of IrY; post-OER shows oxidized surface with ~2 nm thick core-shell structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The well-defined lattice fringes of 0.235 nm from the high-resolution TEM image can be attributed to the (111) plane of IrY (Figure 1e)... post-test IrY exhibits an oxidized surface, and a clear core-shell structure is observed... oxidized shell showed an average thickness of ≈ 2 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir L₃-edge XANES shows higher white-line intensity for IrY vs pure Ir, suggesting higher Ir valence state due to electronic interaction with Y.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) at the Ir L₃-edge revealed a marginally higher white-line (WL) intensity for the IrY catalyst when compared to pure Ir, suggesting a higher Ir valence state and cationic environment due to the electronic interaction between Ir and doped Y.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir 4f binding energy in IrY positively shifted by 0.2 eV vs pure Ir (61.2 eV for Ir⁰ 4f₇/₂); Y shows 0.5 eV negative shift; post-OER XPS shows formation of Ir⁴⁺ oxidation state alongside metallic Ir⁰; surface Y content ≈33.3%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ir 4f spectra for the as-synthesized catalysts can be deconvoluted into two sets of doublet peaks... binding energy of Ir 4f in IrY is positively shifted by 0.2 eV compared to pure Ir (61.2 eV for Ir⁰ 4f₇/₂ and 64.2 eV for Ir⁰ 4f₅/₂)... significant negative shift of 0.5 eV was observed in the valence state of Y... XPS analysis to approximate the proportion of Y... ≈33.3%... after OER, it exhibits doublet peaks that might be deconvoluted to form a metallic state peak and an oxidation state peak attributed to Ir⁴⁺.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Ir L₃-edge XANES shows progressive Ir oxidation with increasing potential; FT-EXAFS shows Ir-O bond formation at 1.44 Å and stronger Ir-O covalence in IrY.
nodes.evidence_snippet: we observed that the WL intensity of the IrY catalyst increased with increasing potential... when increasing the potential to 1.4 and 1.6 V, a new bond emerges at 1.44 Å, indicative of the formation of an Ir-O bond.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows γ and ε peaks for Ir⁴⁺-OH and Ir⁴⁺-O species with increasing intensity at higher potentials.
nodes.evidence_snippet: upon the application of potential, the characteristic features of the γ and ε peaks correspond to Ir⁴⁺-OH and Ir⁴⁺-O species, respectively... intensity of the γ and ε peaks gradually increased with increasing potential.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-stability test Ir leaching from IrY catalyst measured at 3.12 wt% vs 26.08 wt% for pure Ir.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the IrY catalyst exhibited a substantially lower Ir leaching percentage, measured at 3.12 wt%, in comparison to pure Ir, which exhibited a leaching percentage of 26.08 wt%.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-catalysis XRD (after 100 h at 10 mA cm⁻²) shows no substantial shifts in peak positions or broadening for IrY.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After the CP test (10 mA cm⁻² for 100 h), we conducted XRD analysis on the post-catalysis IrY, and the results indicated that there were no substantial shifts in peak positions or broadening.
